utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please be seated. The affirmation you made still applies, and we now have some further questions, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mitic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We had before this Court some evidence that Mr. Sainovic called Mr. Djordjevic while Mr. Djordjevic was at the Stimlje police station, and this was on the 15th of January, 1999 when the operation began.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that, sir. I didn't say that he spoke to Sainovic. These are your words.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, they are. Mr. Mitic, I'm just telling you for the time being the evidence, and I want to show you something and then ask you some questions about it.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'd like to bring up 00605, that's the Prosecution 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Mitic, Mr. Sainovic was interviewed by members of the OTP and he answered some questions. I'd like to show what you his answers were in that regard, and ask you some questions about these answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go to page 723 of this interrogatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The record or the transcript of the taped interview, Mr. Mitic, record has both the English translation of what Mr. Sainovic said as well as what he said in Serbian, so I had like you to read what he said. In particular, while you were reading what I show you, I want you to focus on the circumstances in which Mr. Sainovic said he called, the date, and the place he called. So for this page you can have a look at all of it to get your context, but I'm particularly interested in what is in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know if you could pan it so the witness could see the entire page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When you are through, you can let us know, Mr. Mitic. You are through with that page?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the next page I think you only need to focus on the last two or three answers of Mr. Sainovic on the next page, which is page 725 of the record. And for this part, can you read all of page 726. That's the next page. Again I ask you to focus on time, date, circumstances, and who he says he calls. Having regard to what you just read, Mr. Mitic, do you not now recall that -- well, let me break it up into two bits. Firstly, that Mr. Sainovic -- sorry, that Mr. Djordjevic was at the Stimlje police station on the 15th, the morning of the 15th, I'm not asking about whether or not he was there on the 18th, he might have been there or the 18th or not, I don't know about that, I'm asking about the 15th. Do you not now recall that he was there on the morning of the 15th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. What I remember is the 18th because the chief of SUP ordered me in his presence to carry out my task, and that's why I remember. Nothing else. I don't remember anything about the 15th or better, I did not see General Djordjevic on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not asking about the 18th, he might have been there on the 18th as well. But the 15th, focus on the morning of the 15th. Do you not recall that that morning Mr. Djordjevic received at least one telephone call from Mr. Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I can tell you how often I saw General Djordjevic in my career. I saw him twice, and I exactly remember only the 18th, and I -- the first time I saw General Djordjevic was in 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was attending a management course. He taught us the subject of organisation and functioning --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's interesting, but take the date out and let's just focus on the call. Whatever date it was, do you not recall that Mr. Sainovic called Mr. Djordjevic while he was there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, believe me. On the 18th I took the on-site investigation team to Racak. When we returned, I didn't see General Djordjevic again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: At that time who or what position did Mr. Sainovic occupy?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me that I can't tell exactly. I know that he was the representative of the cabinet of the Republic in Kosovo and Metohija. Whether he was in a co-ordination body or something, I really don't know, but I know that he had an official position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And at that time -- well, on the 15th, was it correct that Mr. Lukic was in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I didn't see General Lukic. I know that the chief of the SUP contacted the staff several times. Whether he spoke to General Lukic or someone else, I don't know, because I didn't have any close ties with General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it your evidence, Mr. Mitic, that at no time did you discover that Mr. Lukic directed Mr. Sainovic to call the Stimlje police station for any reason?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, believe me, this is the first time I've heard of it. Never have I heard that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we move into private session. I wish to ask some questions about a particular witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: (redacted

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Mitic, you said, if I could find it, at 12714, that when they were -- or the procedure in respect to the anti-terrorist actions within your police area, was that the chief of the secretariat compiled a proposal and sent it to the staff, namely, to arrest terrorists, in this case we are speaking of Ivaja, Kotlina, and Pustenik, and the action was carried out, and you said that you knew that the Urosevac company of the PJP took part, and to quote, you said, "I'm not sure but I think it was also the PJP up the Miljani [phoen] SUP and members of the army." You recall that there was some co-ordination with the VJ in respect to some of the operations, anti-terrorist operations that were conducted by the Urosevac police?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question. Could you be more precise. I didn't really understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is it not true that some anti-terrorist operations that the police from the Urosevac SUP were of involved in also involved a co-ordinated assistance of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, if this refers to Ivaja Kotlina, that area there, I have already explained that a PJP company from Urosevac participated. I'm not sure, but I think there was also a company from Gnjilane, and some soldiers from the Urosevac barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, let me ask, don't you recall, or do you recall that there were MUP anti-terrorist actions where the MUP acted in co-ordination with the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will repeat. The PJP received assignments from the staff. How they regulated those relations, I don't know. I'm not aware of that. An order arrived that a PJP company from Urosevac should participate. They left to carry out their task, and they reported to whoever it was that sent them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but right throughout your testimony, you have been telling us about stuff you know even when you are not there. And you've been telling us about what has been communicated to you by your SUP chief. I'm just asking you, do you not know that in some of these anti-terrorist operations, the VJ co-ordinated with the MUP in Urosevac SUP area?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat, Mr. Prosecutor, I don't know what their precise role was. I do remember who participated, but how this was regulated in the plan, I don't know, because I did not participate in drawing up the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I think -- so I think based on what you are saying, your answer is yes, there were co-ordinated actions with the VJ and the MUP, but you don't know how this was regulated in the plan because you did not participate in drawing up the plan; is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. They did participate in that particular action, but what the role of the various participants was, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thanks. These plans you said would you drawn up by the staff in Pristina and was sent to your SUP chief; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the plan was not sent to the SUP chief. He only received notification that the unit should get ready and follow that assignment. The company commander got his orders from the staff, whether he actually went to the staff in Pristina or whether the orders were delivered to him in some way, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think you told earlier that Colonel Jelic was a commander of the 243rd Brigade in Urosevac. Did he meet with your SUP chief from time to time in respect to these co-ordinated anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They knew each other and met often privately, but as for this concrete -- this specific operation, I don't know whether they met and made agreements about operations. Nor did Jelic's entire unit take part. For him to take part in the organisation of the rest. One of his officers took part in one combat group, but not the entire barracks. That's why Jelic wasn't in a position to talk to Bogi. It was the staff that made such decisions and passed on the decisions to the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know if a meeting, that is, Mr. Jelic meeting with your SUP chief at any time in respect to any anti-terrorist action that the MUP proposed to take part in, and that's apart from the Racak operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I told you about Racak. I know you are now returning to Racak again. Speaking of Kotlina one time and Racak another time. Except for a briefing, there was no other meeting to make arrangements about Racak. And as for Ivaja, there was no reason for Janicijevic to meet Jelic about it because they didn't plan the action, the staff had planned the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When there was a requirement for the MUP or the PJP from Urosevac to participate in an action, you said Mr. Janicijevic, your SUP chief would be notified. Would he tell you about this, or how did he become aware of the notification that the Urosevac PJP were supposed to be engaged in an action?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the chief of the secretariat having learned of the use of the PJP would pass on to me who was the chief of the department of the police the information to pass on to the commanders of the police station, because members of the PJP from Urosevac, Kacanik, Strpce, and Stimlje were there, and I believe that one or two squads were even provided by the traffic police station. So I was duty-bound, either me or my officer in charge of these jobs, to prepare a unit, that is a squad or a platoon or whatever, and send the people to this specific location with the technical equipment that is, vehicles, gear, et cetera. And my task is accomplished when they inform me how many people they sent there and once they report to Lecic who was the company commander. That's where I'm out of it. Then I informed the chief of the SUP that the unit arrived there in full strength or that possibly someone was missing, and that Lecic continued to carry out activities in accordance with the plan which was adapted by the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And in the course of this organisation that you were involved in, you don't know of any meetings between any VJ personnel and your SUP chief in respect to the carrying out of these anti-terrorist operations or actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm just asking --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, they never had meetings, I mean, the chief of the SUP and a representative of the army because they didn't plan the actions. The chief of the SUP merely sent proposal to the staff concerning the problems in the field. And the proposal was actually a security assessment, or rather, the security assessment was part of it. So this proposal was submitted to the staff, and the staff then plans the activities to -- subsequent activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that in respect to the Racak operation, Mr. Jelic was present at one of the briefings solely so that you would know what was going on to avoid the consequences of a friendly fire even though it is your testimony that the VJ did not participate in the Racak operation. In those other operations or actions that involved the co-ordinated action of both the VJ and the MUP, can you tell us how was this co-ordinated in Urosevac?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how, let me repeat. Lecic got his assignment from the staff in Pristina, and I suppose, but I cannot be certain, that the military commander, the leader of the combat group or whatever we may choose to call it, received some instructions, but not from Jelic, but from Pristina. He received a plan of engagement, possibly even from Jelic, I wouldn't know. But that was the chain of command that was in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at P947 quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Mitic, while it's coming up, did you do your military service?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. While I attended secondary police school -- or rather, the fact that I attended secondary police school was counted as if I had served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In any case, I'm going to show you a couple of VJ documents, and I hope that you might be able to assist us.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certainly, if I know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a regular combat report from Colonel Jelic of the 243rd Brigade to the Pristina Corps Command of the 13th of April, 1999. And if you look at item 1.2 it indicates: "Pursuant to a decision of 12 April 1999, a blockade was implemented and in an ensuing concerted action with the Urosevac PJP company, the STS," and that is the terrorists, "in the Firaj, Brod, and Slatina sector were crushed and destroyed." Do you remember this action in mid-April, 1999? Do you remember dispatching the PJP from Urosevac to take part in this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I don't remember all details, but I remember the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you go on the scene of the operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know whether or not the MUP entered or the PJP company of the MUP entered Slatina and Brod?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me that I am not acquainted with the details of the operation. I don't remember them. Whether they entered Firaj and Brod, I don't know, because these places are in Strpce municipality. Firaj, Brod, yes, it's that municipality, whereas Slatina I believe belongs to the Kacanik municipality. But believe me, I don't remember the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at P767.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: A Joint Command order of the 15th of April, 1999, strictly confidential number 455-152. If we go to the last item or the last paragraph of item 4, we could just see what the operation it relates to, or the date of the operation it relates to. And that is on page 4 in the English copy. This is for the 24th of April, 1999, 0600 hours. And I think you can see there on your copy. And if you go back to the first page, first paragraph of item 1. It tells you about the area where this operation is focused on or the villages in the general area of Mount Jezersko villages are Budakovo, Jezerce, Nerodimlje, Petrovo and Plesina. If we could move on to the second paragraph, paragraph 2. It basically says that the task of the Pristina Corps with reinforcements from armed non-Siptar population was to support the MUP in routing and destroying the STS in the general area of Jezerce, Budakovo. Have a look at the entire paragraph. I don't wish to read it. My question is, do you remember this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And were the PJP from Urosevac involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the operation to some extent, but I cannot state with any degree of certainty who took part in it. Budakovo belongs to the Suva Reka municipality. Jezerce, Nerodimlje, Petrovo, and Plesina are in the Urosevac municipality. I vaguely remember, but I couldn't really tell you with any degree of certainty who exactly took part in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But wouldn't it be likely that the Urosevac PJP would be involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And can I ask if you -- if you went on -- went in the area where those villages are located, where the Urosevac PJP would have been engaged at?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, when this operation was first conducted in the mountains of Jezerce, I went to an area called Sastav Reka [phoen] but that's at the foot of mount Jezerce. We had observation points there, and that's as far as I went, I didn't go any further. Except for an on-site investigation which I attended once, but that was -- had nothing to do with this operation. The first time operation Jezerce was conducted, that's when it was, but I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Talking about the 23rd of April and thereafter. Very well. Let's move to another document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, line -- page 23, line 24, the word "non-" should be inserted before Siptar population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, thank you very much, Your Honours. Could we look at P956, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That document, if we see the first page here, it's a war diary of the 243rd Mechanised Brigade which we got from the Pristina Corps archives. It's from the 24th of March, 1999 to the 10th of June. And if we could move to page 7 in English, and that is an entry for the 31st of March. If we can get that entry in B/C/S. While we are getting it up, Mr. Mitic, was it sometimes, or was it the responsibility of the police, according to law, the law then in force, to direct volunteers to their various military -- or the military establishments to which they should go to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Could you please explain what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If persons wanted to volunteer to fight in the war, what would the responsibilities of the MUP do in respect to these persons? Could the MUP accept these volunteers, or would you be required to transfer them somewhere else, and I am talking about according to law, not what actually happened?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you see, we didn't have volunteers in our ranks, we had the reserve police force. We had active-duty police officers and the reserve police force. We have never had volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So did you direct volunteers who wanted to fight, or was it your duty to direct them to the appropriate VJ recruitment centre in your area?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they never contacted us. Nobody contacted the police if they were volunteer. You saw from earlier documents that check-points were set up at the administrative border with Serbia proper, so such units were held back, not even individuals could pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, the first entry for this day, the 31st of March is that: "Volunteers keep arriving at the unit. They are issued with equipment and assigned to units immediately." I think the Court has heard evidence that that would be the responsibility of the police would be to direct volunteers to the VJ according to law, so I'll just ask you this: Did you know that volunteers were being incorporated into the 243rd Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, I'm not privy to that. I've only heard it now from you. In going about my tasks and doing my work, I never heard of anybody contacting us and being referred to the army. I don't know of any such instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. If we could look to the bottom of the page in English, I think we need to go to the next page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It says: "Part of a combat group and the reinforced tank company have been engaged in providing support to MUP forces along the following axes: Blace village, Tumicina village, Banja village, Semetiste village, Kravasarija village. It's an operation on the 31st of March, 1999. Do you recall whether or not MUP units from Urosevac SUP participated in this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These places are outside the territory of my secretariat. I'm not sure to which municipality they belong. Well, if that was a task, probably, probably the units were involved. But I wouldn't know because these villages are not on my territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we look at page 8 in English, and I think it would be the next page in B/C/S. But I want to see the entry for the 1st of April, [Realtime transcript read in error "February"] 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It says TG, I think it means tactical group, and the reinforced tank company from tactical group 252 have been engaged in providing support to MUP forces along the axes of the same villages: Blace village, Tumicina village, Banja village, and Semetiste village, Kravasarija village. To so operation continued on to the next day. Do you know where those villages are, in which municipality?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know apart from Blace, there is a village by that name in the Kacanik municipality, but I really don't know these other villages. So this may be an area which I'm not familiar with. But in Kosovo, I suppose that there are several villages by the same name as Blace.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, if this is a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is, Mr. Stamp. Page 27, line 4, February should be April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. We adjourn now and resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could move to page 12 of this document, and we are still on the war diary of the 243rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Entry for the 6th of April, do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It says: "From 0630 hours to 1600 hours, the batch of the mixed anti-tank artillery battalion and the PJP sealed off the villages of Kamena Glava and another village, which is illegible. The STS offered weak resistance in the sector and the villages were mopped up. Two hunting rifles were seised." Can you assist us, can you make out which village that is, it says, "sealed off the villages of Kamena Glava and another village?"

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't really. I can't read the name of this village.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. But in so as far as Kamena Glava is involved -- is referred to, do you recall that on the 6th of April, the PJP from Urosevac was involved in an operation there, do you recall that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember it vaguely, but I can't say for certain anything about it. I remember something happened in Kamena Glava, I don't recall the name of the other village, nor do I remember any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Could we see if we can look at these places that we just discussed on a map?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you look at P823. That's the Kosevo atlas and if we could go to page 18, which is a map of the area, of the Urosevac area, or part of it. Can we pan out a little bit. Let's try to work with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know or can you point out where Slatina and Brod is?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, I think you've circled -- put two circles on the map, one of them --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slatina is the first one, and Brod is the second one. I think they are there but the writing is quite small.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I think we'll have to expand this a little bit so we can be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could mark them again, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And you see Vata there as well to the east of Slatina, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you just put a circle or an oval around these three villages, Brod, Slatina, Vata?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you circle them, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The -- this looks to me to be about, what, 8, 10 kilometres from Urosevac as the crow flies, Mr. Mitic. You agreed with me earlier that the PJP from Urosevac was involved in an operation there on the 13th of April. We have evidence from somebody by the name of Sesdi Lama [phoen] who testified that at about that time, at about the 13th of April, forces of the FRY and Serbia, that is the VJ paramilitaries, et cetera, entered those villages and killed many inhabitants and set the others -- and forced the others to leave. Did you not receive any information about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that there were any paramilitaries on the territory of my secretariat. I'm hearing it for the first time now from you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you hear that security forces from the FRY and Serbia entered those villages on the 13th, killed many of the villagers, and expelled the remainder?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never heard that. If there was an anti-terrorist action, it's possible that terrorists got killed in those operations, but that there was an action to drive out the people, I never heard that. I'm hearing if for the first time from you. And you mentioned paramilitary forces, I don't know what you meant by that, because there were no such forces on our territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Ever heard of a Serbian Chetnik movement?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they existed in World War II. I know such a movement existed in history, but it's not true that they existed on my territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. We'll get to that shortly. When, for example, this operation that we spoke of the 13th of April, when Mr. Lecic returned to the Urosevac police station after an operation like this, did he have to give a report as to the casualties that might have occurred as a result of an operation like this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lecic submitted a report most probably to his command or to the staff. He did not submit any report to the Urosevac SUP. In these three villages, well, to be quite honest, I don't remember the action there, unless it was an action when a military convoy was attacked because I know that something was done then, but I think another village was in question. I don't know. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yeah, but when I showed you the order of the combat report in respect of that operation you said you knew about it and your Urosevac PJPs were involved in that operation. In any case, the question is this, after your PJPs were involved in an operation, did they not report as to whether or not there were any civilian casualties, and that is report to your SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, if people got killed in the operation, most probably a team was sent out to carry out an on-site investigation, and then the crime investigation department of the police would have been notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So they would have had to file reports about civilians who are killed in the operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of whether they were civilians or terrorists, if there are casualties in an operation, most probably the criminal investigation police would have been called upon to carry out an on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Could you find on this map Kamena Glava for me. It's another place where we saw that there were VJ and MUP co-ordinated action.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is Kamena Glava, although the writing is quite small.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think you have it there. Also called Komogllave in Albanian we can see.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Komogllave, that's the Albanian name. In Albanian, you say Komogllave, and in Serbian you say Kamena Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We saw the report just now, just before the break, of this co-ordinated action, of a co-ordinated action of the VJ and the MUP in which they mopped up Kamena Glava on the 6th of April, 1999. And we have evidence before the Court, Mr. Mitic, from Florim Krasniqi that on the 7th and around the 7th of April, he saw that village and the surroundings on fire. The houses had been burnt, or were burning. Do you know about that, Mr. Mitic, that these village, the villages in Kamena Glava were torched in the course of this operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as for Kamena Glava, I remember there was an action that was carried out. I don't remember the details, but I do know from before that we always had the worst extremists in Kamena Glava, and many KLA members came from that village. I think they set up a sort of nucleus there and spread to the surrounding villages, so this action was carried out in order to arrest these terrorist groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm talking to you about evidence from Krasniqi, Florim that at the time of this operation, he saw the village on fire, and in addition to that, another witness, Bedri Hyseni said that at the time of this operation, the 6th of April, people were expelled from Kamena Glava and its surroundings. Did Mr. Lecic or any of the PJPs from Urosevac mention any such thing to you, the expulsion of the civilians and the torching of the civilian houses in these villages at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where there is fighting, where there is action, of course some houses catch fire from the fighting, either from mortar shells, hand-held mortars, or other weapons because the Albanian terrorists had both mortars and hand-held rocket-launchers. They had heavy weapons. So that was certainly a consequence of the fighting, but as for expulsions, believe me, I cannot give you any information about other areas, but with respect to the area covered by the Urosevac SUP, we did our utmost to make sure that no one expelled people or forced them to leave. I explained that I personally went to the railway station to talk to the people and to tell them to take shelter and not to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. That is what you are saying you did. Just let's focus on Kamena Glava. You are saying that there was fighting and the terrorist had these weapons, but that is not the evidence we have before the Court from the witnesses in respect of this area, and I'll reread to you the combat report that I just showed you from the 243rd Brigade for that day. It says: "From 630 to 1600 hours, the mixed anti-tank artillery battalion and the PJP sealed off the villages of Kamena Glava and another illegible village. The STS offered weak resistance in the sector and the villages were mopped up. Two hunting rifles were seised. Two terrorists were killed." This reports indicates to me that there was not much resistance, and it was the VJ supporting the MUP that had the heavy artillery. So the --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not correct, in Kamena Glava perhaps they didn't have a heavy artillery but they certainly did in the surrounding villages, and I can't recall the names of the villages around Kamena Glava in the direction of Kacanik, but they were linked to the area of Vitina municipality, and from there, they fired because there may not have been strong forces in Kamena Glava itself, but there were in the neighbouring villages, and they knew that they had a few fellow fighters in Kamena Glava so they fired on the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's focus on Kamena Glava. These two witnesses mentioned Kamena Glava, torching of the civilian houses, expulsion of the civilian population in the course of that operation, or at least on those dates. You are saying you never received any reports from any PJP from either Mr. Lecic or anybody else about this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and there were no expulsions. I can affirm that there were no expulsions because we all did our utmost to prevent this happening in our area. There were people transiting through our area because there's railway station there and there were vehicles bringing people from other places.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could, Your Honours, could this point map be -- this marked map be received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this manner of marking the map. Mr. Stamp says mark these villages and the witness marks them and then he puts questions about things the witness did not say but about other documents. I think Mr. Stamp could have circled these villages himself and the witness could have commented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Many times, Mr. Djurdjic, with both Prosecution and Defence, questions witnesses have identified on maps, the locations by circling the named towns. That's all this is doing. The Chamber will receive this marked map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the map will be Exhibit P01556.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could look at page 17 of P823.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you said, Mr. Mitic, that during the Jezerce operation, that was referred to in one of the documents I showed you, you went to -- to a village in the foothills. If we could just pause, Mr. Mitic, I'll find precisely what you said.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not a village, Mr. Prosecutor. It's a place called --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'll find it. You were telling us what place you went to, that would help?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sastav Reka this is where two rivers flow together, coming from two different directions, it's a confluence actually of two rivers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. You said that "that's at the foot of mount Jezerce. We had observation points there, and that's as far as I went. I didn't go any further." Can you remember about when it is that you went here, was this at about the time of the operation, and I remind you that the operation according to the combat order was on the 23rd of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I was -- in 1998 I was there when the first terrorist action was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when you said you went to an area called Sastav Reka, that was in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The first anti-terrorist action.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, in the course of the operation in April 1999, did you go there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We've had evidence before the Court of torching of Albanian villages and deportations of Albanian civilians from the villages in that area. Did you receive any reports from any of your PJP commanders about any such thing?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this area of Jezerska Planina and the village of Jezerce, all this was a terrorist base. The civilian population had gone to the town of Urosevac to stay with friends and relatives long before these anti-terrorist actions. In 1998 and 1999, these people were living in Urosevac, so they could not have been expelled from these villages because they had already moved out and gone to stay with friends in Urosevac. They stayed in an area of town in the direction of the village of Nerodimlje, we had information about that, and they didn't dare go back to their villages because of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's firstly identify where we are. Do you see the villages that were referred to in that Joint Command order? Do you know where Budakova is? Can you make out where Budakova is?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the municipality of Suva Reka. It's not my territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but you remember that the order referred to -- I think you did say you recalled the action, referred to axis including that village but also villages in your SUP? Can you find where Plesina is? That was the next one that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plesina. There's lower and upper Plesina, which do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You were telling us that you recalled the action. Do you recall the action which Plesina did the action involve?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it must have been Gornja Plesina, upper Plesina. But they are almost one village, they are only a few hundred metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you see the area? Can you circle the area?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jezerce is here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Plesina?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plesina, I can't seem to be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If you go down 6 kilometre to the east, south-east of Jezerce?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And above that to the north about 3 kilometres, Nerodimlje?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But, you know, I don't know in which context Nerodimlje was mentioned, but there couldn't have been any fighting there, only in Donje Nerodimlje near the woods there are some -- some buildings or maybe hamlets that may have been the site of fighting, but Gornje Nerodimlje couldn't have been a site of fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am happy to see that you know where there was fighting from where there was not. So, therefore, you should be able to tell us this: Were villages, villages and hamlets, in the surrounding area of all these towns torched during these operations or actions in the period following the 24th of March?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, not at Gornje Nerodimlje. That was a mixed village with Albanian and Serb population. As far as Plesina is concerned, most probably in the course of combat, there were -- there may have been damaged houses, but certainly there was no massive burning of houses. And at Nerodimlje, there were -- there was fierce anti-terrorist fighting as early as 1998, but it's not true that there was massive burning of houses and the expulsion of population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let's be clear, for my part let's say we accept that there were KLA, the KLA had strongholds in some of these areas, particularly Jezerce and Nerodimlje, because that's the evidence we've heard, but did you receive any information that there was wide-scale torching of Albanian hamlets and villages throughout this area?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you, it's possible that in that mountainous area toward the woods up there, Gornja Plesina, where there was fighting that there may have been damaged houses, but there was no massive burning of houses. And as for Jezerce, I don't know how much was destroyed, in the earlier anti-terrorist operations because they offered strong resistance in all directions. The stronghold was in Jezerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. That's the distinction I'm trying to get you to focus on. Not just damaged houses but torching of entire villages and hamlets. Within the entire area of the SUP Urosevac, did you ever receive any report as to the torching of homes of Kosovo Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only in anti-terrorist operations when there was combat. So some houses were damaged during combat, but there was no massive torching.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, if I could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And before we move on, could this document also be received in evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01557.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You told us earlier that the SUP chief had dual responsibility or shared responsibility along with the field commanders for grave breaches of discipline when the PJPs were engaged in the field, or can I just read the evidence because I want to avoid any ... page 12631: "If a grave violation" and Your Honours, the record actually says grey violation, but I think based on my note it should be grave violation. "If a grave violation or breach of official duty occurred, the commander in the field takes all necessary measures to establish the facts involved and after that he informed chief of the SUP and submits a proposal to initiate disciplinary proceedings." And the next question was "and then the SUP where that person is from would conduct disciplinary proceedings." And your answer was "yes, correct." Next question: "Within a PJP unit be it at the level of a detachment or company, were there any disciplinary organs or not?" And you said "no, there weren't." When a PJP unit in the field or the command of a PJP unit in the field has information that this grave violation occurred, what was the formal requirement for him in informing the SUP chief? Would he have to do so in writing, was there a requirement that he should report it in writing, that's my question?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you actually asked several questions but I'll make an effort to provide an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'll withdraw everything else I said, and ask you, having regard to what I quoted about what you just said, that the commander in the field takes all necessary measures to establish the facts involved and after that inform the chief of the SUP and submits a proposal to initiate disciplinary proceedings, was this submission done in writing?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a serious breach of official responsibility was committed nobody was in better position to establish that then the commander in the field or if he was absent, then his deputy or another commanding officer, and if it was established as a fact, it was called different -- it was called differently earlier than it was today. But anyway, once the relevant facts and circumstances were established, but company commander files a disciplinary report against the police officer and forwards it to the SUP chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it seems pretty much logical from what you are saying that this disciplinary report that is filed is in writing?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: While you were chief of the OUP for Urosevac, did you see any such disciplinary reports from the PJP commanders in respect to MUP members committing crimes like torching of houses or murder against Kosovo Albanian civilians?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know something, whether or not such disciplinary report was filed of that kind, I don't remember, but I don't think so. But there were disciplinary reports even criminal proceedings or misdemeanour proceedings were launched against some officers on other grounds, such as theft, abuse of official position, or the like, but what you said, no, no such cases are known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know of any policemen from your SUP be engaged to participate in escorting trains or civilians through Urosevac towards the border, that is, during the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- just allow me to finish. The police station, there was a police station for the escort of vehicles at Kosovo Polje. They were the only police officers who could accompany or escort trains. No other police officers did what you were inquiring about. So there was a police station for escorting trains at Kosovo Polje, that was their specific task. They escorted trains that went in the direction of Belgrade or, but I'm not really familiar with what exactly they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. So I take it that the Urosevac police were not involved in escorting trains, that was the police from Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm saying that the Urosevac police played no part in that. I don't know when the police from Kosovo Polje escorted anybody or where to. I cannot really say anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Apart from being the PJP commander for those units in Urosevac, Mr. Lecic was also deputy commander of the Urosevac SUP, am I correct? And that is in 1999.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it was, when he had no work as a PJP member, then his regular duty was that of the deputy commander of the Urosevac police station. So when he wasn't busy in the PJP, he went about his regular work at the police station in Urosevac.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when he about his regular work, he reported to you and through you to the SUP chief; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it was, he was deputy commander, and he carried out the orders of his commander and I as chief of the department of the police. You said OUP several times, but I wasn't chief of that. I was chief of the department of the police. And I communicated directly with the commanders and monitored their work, their activities, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So when Lecic was involved in the field and was engaged in the regular duties in Urosevac, who did he report to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we must keep these things apart. While he was busy as a PJP member, he reported to the staff of the MUP in Pristina. And when he was carrying out his regular work and regular tasks, he reported to the commander of the police station and that was Vukasin Damjanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And who did the commander of the police station report to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you a minute ago, but I can repeat. The commanders of police stations were responsible to me and I was responsible to the chief of the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have a look at some documents that you were shown. I'm not -- let's look at one or two of them. I don't think we need to go through all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You were shown many dispatches signed by Mr. Djordjevic and the first question you were asked was which SUPs they were addressed to, and your answer invariably was to all of them, all 33 of them. But I also notice, and I am not going to bother going through these documents, there are about ten of them with you. You also notice that they are also addressed to the MUP staff Pristina, to the head, did you also see that? And we are now looking at P1205.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said. To all SUPs from 1 through 33 in the Republic of Serbia and to the staff of the MUP in Pristina that is to the chief there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You are saying that last part now that it's also addressed to the chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe we could look at another one, P1206.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Similarly, you see this is addressed not only to the 33 SUP chiefs but also to the MUP staff in Pristina, to the head. You see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I can tell you that, you know, the other documents that you were shown including D438, P1207, P717 and some others that you were asked about the SUPs they were addressed to, they were also addressed to the chief or the head of the MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to P717.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Similarly addressed to all 33 MUP chiefs as well as the chief of the MUP staff in Pristina among others. Shall we go to page 2 in both the English and the B/C/S. If you look at the first paragraph that starts on page 2 in B/C/S, and this would be the third paragraph that starts on page 2 in English, let's look at the third and fourth paragraph in English that starts on page 2, and the first and second that starts on page 3. I selected these two paragraphs primarily because they relate to police operations in Kosovo in particular. Just read them quickly, and if we could move to page 3 in both B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say paragraph 2, "prevent the spreading of terrorist activities?"

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, the first paragraph that begins on page 2 in the B/C/S, and the second paragraph that begins at page 2 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the prevention of the spreading of terrorist activities of Albanian separatists, especially in the area of AP Kosovo and Metohija, as well as the possible planting of explosive devices at vital industrial traffic, religious sports, residential, catering, and other places of general interest, and places where citizens gather in large number, I believe that's what it says. And the following paragraph says: In the territory of AP Kosovo and Metohija, step up the coverage of facilities and places where Serbs, Montenegrins, and members of the nationalities loyal to the Republic of Serbia and the FR of Yugoslavia often gather in large numbers."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we move on, I just wanted to settle an issue of translation, so I was going to ask you to read the first part of the first paragraph slowly again because I just want to be clear about one aspect, whether it says inside or outside Kosovo. Could you just reread that please, and we'll have a translation.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prevent the spreading of terrorist activities by Albanian separatists especially in AP Kosovo and Metohija, as well as the possible planting of explosive devices at vital industrial, et cetera, facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just mention that because, Your Honours just for the record, there's an error in the English version where it says outside. It should be inside or in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And at page 43, line 21, all 33 SUP chiefs is what should be read instead of all 33 MUP chiefs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I ask this paragraph to be enlarged to enable the witness to read it. I mean, the one to which Mr. Stamp is referring now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it can be seen better now because previously the letters were quite small. "Prevent the spreading of terrorist activities of Albanian separatists, especially outside the area of AP Kosovo and Metohija..."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, counsel. And if we could move to page 3. In English it would be the third paragraph, in B/C/S it would be the first paragraph that begins on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You can read that one to yourself. You don't need to read that one aloud.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say the first one or the marked paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, the first paragraph that begins on that page. First bullet point that begins on that page. Mr. Mitic, weren't all the addressees of this order responsible to comply with the order of General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were all duty-bound to do so, to act in accordance with this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And similarly with the other dispatches that Mr. Djordjevic issued, they were duty-bound to comply with those orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they weren't always orders. Sometimes for the purpose of informing some services, it doesn't have to be orders every time. We didn't receive orders all the time. Sometimes we received information as to what should be done, step up security measures to secure facilities or whatever. This was just about reminding us of our legal obligations, they weren't orders strictly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But when they were orders, the addressees were duty-bound to comply with these orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions in the dispatch must be carried out, so we must act in accordance with it. I don't know which order you mean specifically, to secure facilities, to step up the activities of the police, something else maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I remind you that some of the orders or dispatches from General Djordjevic were addressed to General Lukic, and you said all the addressees were duty-bound to act in accordance therewith. On what basis would Mr. Lukic be duty-bound to act in accordance with the orders issued by General Djordjevic? What is your basis for saying that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what, in my opinion this was for information for the staff to be aware of everything and everybody did their job, but the staff was in charge of following all the activities in Kosovo, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just listen to my question. You said that the addressees had been duty-bound to comply with the orders of General Djordjevic. We see that the head of the staff General Lukic was an addressee, and I'm merely asking on what basis would General Lukic be obliged to comply with General Djordjevic's orders?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to explain this to you. General Lukic was informed for his information so that he could monitor whether the SUPs on the territory of Kosovo and Metohija had complied with the dispatch. General Lukic was at the head of the staff but the staff could not carry out all these measures and activities on its own, so it was his duty to follow whether all the secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija had acted on the instructions in the dispatch. That was his only duty. You couldn't explain everybody's duty in the dispatch because it was addressed to all of them, but his role would have been to control the carrying out of the instructions in the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if a SUP chief failed to carry out the instructions or failed to carry out the instructions properly, what is your understanding that Mr. Lukic should do about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Lukic, if chiefs of SUPs in Kosovo and Metohija failed to carry out the instructions in the dispatch, would have initiated disciplinary measures against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: How would General Lukic initiate disciplinary measures against SUP chiefs? Who would he address it to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never heard that any such thing ever actually happened, and everybody had to comply with the Law on the Interior. All authorised officials were equally responsible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed to something else quickly. Were there reserve police squads in the police area of the Urosevac SUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reserve police force within the Urosevac SUP was the one envisaged in the plan, and they were engaged as needed, but no units were ever formed. They simply carried out the regular duties within the scope of the police stations. They were never used in any anti-terrorist actions. They only carried out regular tasks and assignments, together with active-duty policemen. They never carried out any activity on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think you are talking about reserve policemen in contradistinction to active-duty policemen. But do you know of persons in Serb villages who were armed for the purpose ostensibly of defending those villages and they were called, or the groups of them were called reserve police squads? Do you know of those?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were reserve police squads who were securing their villages. That's what I stated. Their village or their street. These were people who were not in the reserve police force, but you know how it was, a military conscript was anyone who had done his military service and then he could have been liable either for military service or for service in the police. These members of the reserve police squads could have been reservists in the police who had not been activated at that point in time, or they could have been reserve soldiers not activated at the time, and these people might have been in the reserve police squads. Nobody paid them, they did not have health insurance or any pension insurance or any kind of remuneration. Their task was simply to guard their own villages or streets and watch over the safety of the people living in those villages or in those streets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say that there was a problem with interpretation. We did not get the proper interpretation for reserve police squad in our headphones, but it's entered correctly in the transcript. It's correct in the English version, reserve police squad, RPO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could look at P901.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is an order of the then-Pristina Corps Commander General Pavkovic, dated the 26th of June, 1998. If you look at paragraph 2, he says, distribute automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, light machine-guns, sniper rifles, and necessary communications equipment to military conscripts. Do you recall that these were the weapons that were distributed to these RPOs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with this document. It was not available to me, but I do remember, yes, I can't recall what year that was in, but I think in an earlier period it was through the All People's Defence that some weapons were distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, this is the 26th of June, 1998. If you look at the third paragraph, second paragraph, on the basis of the list, the lists are referred to in the first paragraph of item 3, on the basis of the list "... call up military conscripts in small groups to the army barracks or organise distribution and issue of weapons in Serbian and Montenegrin villages. Devote special attention to security measures, secrecy, and camouflage discipline in carrying out this task." Were you aware firstly that these weapons were distributed to persons in Serb and Montenegrin villages?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't just distributed to Serbs and Montenegrins. Weapons were distributed to some Albanians as well. All those guarding villages or streets in towns. All those who were under threat from Albanian terrorists were given weapons. There were Roma who were given weapons, so it wasn't just Serbs and Montenegrins.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This doesn't seem to -- what I trying to remember the expression, well, you know, loyal. This doesn't refer to loyal, non -- or loyal citizens of non-Serbian ethnicity, this refers specifically to Serbs and Montenegrin villages. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what it says here is one thing, but I'm telling you what actually happened, and I'm talking about my area. There were Albanians who were threatened by Albanian terrorists, and they were given weapons. I can even give you some names, if you like. Although it may not be proper to mention their names for their own security.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, tell me about how many Albanians in Urosevac SUP area were armed, just --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the precise numbers but well, 10, 20, it wasn't 100, so several dozen perhaps. But there were whole Roma villages, whole Roma neighbourhoods who were frightened. They came to see the chief of the SUP and said that they felt imperiled, they thought they that they would be attacked by Albanian terrorists, so entire neighbourhoods, Roma neighbourhoods had the weapons distributed to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can you say do you know why this distribution was done in secret, or maybe I should put it this way, do you know why General Pavkovic stated that the distributors should devote special attention to secrecy in this distribution?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I can make an assumption, to avoid panic among the population. When people of any ethnicity saw weapons being distributed, they would panic so most probably that was the reason why, to avoid the spreading of panic among the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could move -- well, if we could look at the last item 6 in English, just the first paragraph. Are aware that the MUP participated in this distribution of weapons to the villages referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Sorry, if we could just move to the second part of item 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But you can read all of it in B/C/S I see, so my question is whether or not you knew of the MUP's participation in this from June 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was done by my office, sir, and we distributed some of the weapons and other weapons were distributed by the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Who had responsibility for monitoring and controlling these reserve police squads, or which organisation had that responsibility?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection, the the commander of each police station was responsible for his area, and where there were members of the reserve police squad. At SUP level, there was an officer in charge of this that was in my squad who was in contact with the commander if they had any information to provide about what they had observed on the ground, then the members of the reserve police squad would inform the commander of the police station who would then forward the information to the officer in charge of the police squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's have a look at P688.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think I must ask you to do that after the break, Mr. Stamp, if that's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honours, yes, Your Honours. And I'm wrapping up, I should indicate to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We were waiting for you to finish this exhibit. We will resume at 10 minutes past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If we could have a look at P769. Sorry, P688. And if we could go straight to page 3 in both of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just to identify where we are, these are the minutes of the meeting of the MUP staff, sorry, in Pristina on the 28th of July, 1998. And this was one attended by the minister, Mr. Stojiljkovic among others, Major-General Lukic, and you'll see near the end of it, indeed you'll also see that chief of the SUP for Urosevac, Bogoljub Janicijevic attended. And could we move straight to page 7 of the English, page 8 of the B/C/S? This is the last paragraph in the English on page 7. Well, while we are there, we see that Mr. Janicijevic gave a presentation at that meeting. If we could move to the last paragraph in English. This is the middle of the page in B/C/S. Captain Pesic made a presentation in respect to the number of squads that were formed and the number of weapons that were issued. He said there were 243 RPOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, where I had indicated earlier with the witness Cvetic when he was here earlier that there was a general mistranslation. It says reserve police station, but it is actually reserve police squads it should be translated to and that weapons were issued to 54.683 persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, do you recall -- let me ask you about your SUP first. Do you recall how many weapons had been distributed in your SUP by July 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Approximately how many?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I can't give you a figure. I simply don't recall the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did Captain or Mr. Janicijevic report to you and other senior members in the SUP on the deliberations at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, most probably he did. He informed us of what had taken place after every meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, do you remember this one in particular?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember he informed us. Can you just tell me the date when this was?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the 29th of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember that he did convey this to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And did he convey to you that the plan was, according to Captain Pesic here in the last sentence of his presentation, that when all this is finished about 60.000 persons have been issued weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell us these details, but as for the number of weapons distributed, I think that this information was sent from our SUP to the staff, it to Blagoj Pesic who was in charge of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could look at P1055.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a report on the visit and meetings held commanders of the RPOs, and it was prepared by Mr. Pesic. I don't think we need to go to the last page. And this is the 16th of February, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could just scroll down in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Meetings were conducted with the relevant or authorised persons from the Urosevac SUP at about 1230 hours on the 16th of February, 1999. Do you recall these meetings where Mr. --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And this is with Mr. Pesic and with Major-General Stojanovic from the staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Momcilo Stojanovic, that's right. Well, if you allow, as far as I remember, I believe that the chief of the SUP, myself, then four commanders of police stations, and I believe the officer in charge of equipment and armaments were present at that meeting. We were about six or seven. That information may be included here, but unless I am mistaken, there were seven of us who attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did any of the RPO commanders attend?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can't remember exactly. I believe that two of them were absent with a justified reason, but the rest were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move to page 8 in the English. Page 7 in the English. Sorry, I'm seeing that it's page 6 that I want.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am looking at the second paragraph here where it says: "The RPO commanders had sent urgent requests to the MUP and other official bodies to take the strictest measures to curb such similar and negative occurrences that affect the unity of Serbs and Montenegrins and undermine the defence of towns and villages." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which paragraph are you referring to? I've read all this, so what are you interested in?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall from what you have seen that the purpose, the prime purpose of these RPOs was to arm the conscripts in Serb and Montenegrin villages?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that wasn't the purpose, Mr. Prosecutor. The purpose was for them to defend themselves against terrorists. They had a fully defensive system.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I see. But it was for Serb and Montenegrin villages to defend themselves, that was the programme in respect of these RPOs?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what, the ones who were in jeopardy, defended themselves. In this specific case they were in jeopardy, but there were also Roma and others who were in jeopardy from the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. If we could look at the chart on page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's take a quick look, particularly on the row for Urosevac. This is an overview of the number of weapons distributed. Is this the information you gave to Captain Pesic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: 36 RPOs, 1.928 weapons, 1.928 weapons issued by the MUP, 3.023 issued by the VJ?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is the information that we sent to Captain Pesic, or rather the officer in charge of these matters, where I sent it to Captain Pesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your evidence, I take it, is that maybe 20 or some dozens, less than 100 Albanians received weapons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Could we look at P85.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This shows a very -- I think you would agree that this is a very important meeting of the MUP staff. The entire leadership of the police is there, we can look at the participants. And in his opening remarks, among other things, General Lukic said, and this is about the third or fourth sentence in General Lukic's opening remarks: "RPO, and that translation again is wrong, it's reserve police squads in nearly all villages inhabited by Serbs are very active. The service has increased its activities in towns." This is the 17th of February, the day after Captain Pesic and General Stanojevic visited the RPOs in Kosovo and issued their report, it's the last document we looked at. Did Mr. Bogoljub Janicijevic, your SUP chief, brief you and others in the SUP about this very important meeting of the 17th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean, but they took measures. Well, clearly the members of these reserve police squads had to be vigilant in their villages because they had to expect terrorist attacks at any given moment, so they had to be vigilant and look out for possible attack against their street or neighbourhood or village. That was their activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But these were -- we were not only talking about the RPOs, we are talking about RPOs in villages inhabited by Serbs, Mr. Mitic; isn't that the true position?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, this isn't combat activity, this is defensive activity of the reserve police squads. They were told to be vigilant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They are vigilant and they ostensibly were to defend villages, but they were --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Serbian villagers who were armed, sir; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not only Serb villages, I said that there were also Roma. I cannot really tell to who exactly the weapons were distributed. That would be guess-work. But I know that entire neighbourhoods in the city were Roma neighbourhoods and that Plaseski Put [phoen] and Urosevac itself there was the Cvetko Kojlovic [phoen] Street on the road to Dugaljovo [phoen], they also requested weapons. And at Bijelinski Put [phoen] there were Roma at several locations who came to ask for weapons because they felt threatened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
