utterances.text: These documents, when I speak about the RPOs, seem to be referring to Serbs and Montenegrins. You were not at all be reminded that it was primarily Serb and Montenegrin citizens or villagers who were armed with these 60.000 weapons? You don't recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I don't know what the documents say, but I remember this extremely well. Weapons were given to everybody who was in jeopardy from the terrorists. Irrespective of their ethnicity, Serbs, Montenegrins, Turks, Roma, whoever felt in jeopardy and who wanted to defend their villages together. There were also Albanians and Serbs who jointly guarded certain streets, yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at P767.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is a joint command order that we looked at before. The Joint Command order for routing and destroying STS forces in the area of Jezerce dated the 15th of April. And if we could go immediately to item 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, there's never been a joint command. You cannot put it that way. I don't know of the existence of a Joint Command ever, at least to my knowledge. I don't know what kind of agreements they made here in the staff, but in the area of my SUP, what you are now trying to put to us, you can believe me when I say that there's never been a joint command. Everybody had their respective tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I wasn't asking about the Joint Command. It says Pristina Corps with the reinforcements and armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija supports the MUP forces in routing and destroying the STS in the area of responsibility. Who were these armed or the members of the armed non-Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question really.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The order for this joint MUP VJ anti-terrorist action refers to the engagement of the armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija in support of the MUP forces. I am asking who were the members of this group, the armed non-Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of language they used. You have to ask them. I cannot answer this question because I don't understand this. I don't know what the author of this report meant. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I suggest to you, Mr. Mitic, that the armed persons, the armed persons of Serbian and Montenegrin ethnicity or armed non-Albanians then, were engaged in some of the anti-terrorist operations with the MUP and the VJ during the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not correct. Most certainly it isn't. I don't know what expression this officer whoever it was used. Armed non-Albanian people, that is not correct. I can tell you the purpose of the reserve police squads. They were under strict control to do only what they were supposed to do and they were never used for any other tasks, any special tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That brings me to my last suggestion. I suggest to you that insofar as many of these armed Serbs or Montenegrin persons, the members of these RPOs committed crimes against the Kosovo Albanian population, it was the responsibility of the police to control them and to prevent this; wouldn't you agree with that at least, that the police were responsible to protect the Albanians from these armed non-Albanian persons?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, it's the duty of the police to protect the citizens from everybody, the terrorists and whoever could threaten their safety. What was the purpose of these reserve police squads? Only to protect themselves, no active duties, only defensive tasks to protect their villages or streets. And it's impossible for anybody to have used such units for anti-terrorist actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know -- well, I think I've asked you before and you've answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Nothing further in cross-examination, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I would first like to ask you, Mr. Mitic, when there's a mobilisation, specifically in times of war, what happens with military conscripts and police conscripts?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When there's a war, everybody acts in accordance with their war time assignment. That's where they are supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did you know whether these RPOs were active after the state of war was declared in 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only repeat that the RPOs sole purpose was to protect themselves against terrorists, to protect their safety and they were not involved in any anti-terrorist actions, I can claim that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you heard of a single case when an RPO member misused this role of protecting their village and committed a criminal offence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see document P767 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, under item 1, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 1 has the heading "enemy," the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And item 2?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The "task of the Pristina Corps."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see item 5.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Unit tasks."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do tell us, under 5.1, to who was the task assigned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: TG 252, the 2nd Armoured, I can't read the rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Whose unit is that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following page of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Under 5.2, to who was this task assigned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the 243rd Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what kind of unit that is?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to the next page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 5.3, can you tell us to who this task was assigned?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the 549th Motorised Brigade -- well, it's a brigade but I don't know the rest of the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What kind of unit is that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see Exhibit P1055. Could now page 7 of the English version be displayed as well as page 5 of the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to know under item 6 there is Urosevac in this table about distributed weapons. Did you have a register of distributed weapons, weapons distributed by the army?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We had separate registers.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you provide this information about the weapons distributed by the army?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, probably it was the staff who provided this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In line 6 of this table, which information were you in a position to give?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in the position to give information about the number of RPOs and the number of weapons issued by the MUP as well as the quantity left in our storage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see pages 7 -- or rather, page 6 of the English version and page 4 of the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp asked you to read the last but one item, or rather, paragraph, about the RPO commanders having sent urgent requests to the MUP and other official bodies to take the strictest measures to curb such and similar negative occurrences. Now, please, tell me, in the previous paragraph what is referred to?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, there were discussions and stories of sorts that some Serbs were selling their houses and leaving Urosevac. There were such comments, such and similar comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And was the MUP in charge of dealing with such requests as put forward in this previous paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most certainly not, but people had various queries and they thought that they had to raise that, but certainly the police couldn't solve their problems, not these problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were there problems because these persons left their villages, problems in defence?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have document P901.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mitic, this is a document issued by the Pristina Corps. Tell me, did you know to whom these weapons were distributed?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably to military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, don't say most probably, but read what it says in item 2.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, to military conscripts. These were persons who had done their military service and who were able bodied.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That you. Did you have anything to do with the distribution of these weapons?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were distributed by the army, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you know how many weapons were distributed and to whom?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't know that because we were members of the police and they were keeping their own records. If we happened to check someone, he would show us the note stating that the weapon had been issued by the military. That's how we knew about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please have P717 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mitic, tell me, in connection with item 1 in this dispatch, what was the reason why this dispatch was sent?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To step up activities because of the upcoming Christmas and New Year holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see that this is a rather long dispatch, did it relate to almost all the lines of work existing in the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, even today such dispatches arrive just ahead of the New Year and Christmas holidays.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us what sort of activity of the ministry is referred to in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Preventive work, stepping up prevention, patrolling certain facilities, squares, streets, and so on, so this dispatch contains instructions for police work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there anything in this dispatch concerning anti-terrorist plans or activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. In fact, there's always something about anti-terrorist activities, yes. So, yes, because even today this is mentioned because there's always a threat of terrorism anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But what measures?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stepping up activities, that is checking person's vehicles, luggage, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is there anything about planned anti-terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see from this dispatch, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in connection with this part shown to you by my learned friend, Mr. Stamp, where it says that in the border areas and in the border belt measures should be taken in co-operation with the Army of Yugoslavia, did you have any connections with the border police?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The border police was responsible to a different administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And was the border police carrying out their regular activities on the border?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to ask you something as follows: Mr. Stamp asked you about the line of reporting when the PJP unit from Urosevac was engaged in anti-terrorist or other tasks. Did you ever receive a report when the PJP unit, or rather, company of the Urosevac SUP was engaged on PJP tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they reported only to whoever engaged them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp asked you whether you received reports on the return of the PJP Urosevac company as to whether Albanian civilian houses have been set on fire, members of the Albanian ethnic minority expelled, so I'd like to know whether you ever received any report that such things were done by the MUP or by the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you ever present on the ground when an anti-terrorist action was being carried out during the war of 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never present there, but when visiting the organisational units, I would learn about the plan, or rather, the chief would of inform narrow circle of us that an anti-terrorist action was being planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive a plan, and did you ever have occasion to see a plan for an anti-terrorist action such as the two or three orders that were shown to you today?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw a plan of that kind. It would be sent to the company command or the commanding officers of the PJP. They would be the ones who would see the plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mitic, do you have any knowledge of any measures of torture, physical maltreatment, or use of electricity and other means against persons brought in for questioning?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR MITIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received any such information nor did anyone ever complain to me of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stamp put to you, I don't want to mention the name, but may I say the number of the witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: He put to you a statement made by Witness K-86. I will now read out to you again page 5125, line 7 to 11:

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Just to avoid errors, I'm wondering if we could just put the passage on the screen because what was read and what was said is not what I have. And I thought there was a misunderstanding early on when there was an objection when I read the passage that I have. So there might be a misunderstanding. If we could just put page 5126 up, line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm doing this for the sake of interpretation. It's possible that Mr. Stamp is right, but both the witness and I received interpretation into Serbian which differed from what was in this line of the transcript, which is why I read it out, 5126, last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may put what is in the transcript to the witness to see whether he agrees with it. Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, while we are waiting for this to come up on the screen, this is a protected witness, so does this have to be redacted from the transcript or not, even though we have not mentioned his name? I understood you to say that we may remain in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The evidence itself was given in closed session so this will need to be private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That completes the questions for you, you will be, I'm sure, pleased to know. We thank you for your attendance here and for the assistance you've been able to give, and you are now free to return to your normal activities. When we rise an officer of the court will show you out. We will now adjourn. The Chamber would thank all the staff who have stayed beyond normal hour to enable this evidence to be completed. We resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25
